task: §C81 Task 9 — verify alt extraction against the in-scope corpus; reconcile the 422-count discrepancy flagged by Task 4 (progress.md line 107) between the design spec's full-corpus census (3,312) and Task 4's corpus sweep (2,890)

inScope: lifraen-efnafraedi — PREVIEW ONLY (17 of 342 source modules — those with extracted segments already present in 02-for-mt/)
scope.outOfScope: lifraen-efnafraedi's other ~325 source modules. Their numbers are reported below ONLY to reconcile the full-corpus (491-module) discrepancy Task 4 flagged; they are not part of this book's in-scope count.

method: Counted by PARSING with @xmldom/xmldom — never by regex over raw XML, per this repo's standing rule. Two independent counting units are reported for every number, and must not be conflated:

countingUnits.rawMediaAltCensus: the number of <media> elements (any nesting depth) carrying a non-empty `alt` (mediaAttrs.alt || the child <image>/<iframe>'s alt), found by parsing each module's <content> with @xmldom/xmldom and reading getAttribute('alt'). This is the design spec's own census method (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-figure-alt-into-pipeline-design.md §1) and is a physical count of source material — it does not know or care what the extractor currently does with each element.
countingUnits.emittedAltSegments: the number of 'alt'-typed segments actually produced by tools/cnxml-extract.js's extractSegments(), called in-memory on this branch (feat/c81-figure-alt) — no CLI run, per the global constraint. This is what the pipeline currently outputs.

rawMediaAltCensus.note: Exact match to the design spec's chemistry row (§1: 627/214/308, sum 1149) and to Task 3's independent DOM-based reproduction of the same figures (task-3-report.md, Finding 2).

emittedAltSegments.note: byPosition here is attributed from the extractor's OWN structure object (structure.inlineMedia[] = para-inline; a structure.content figure node's media = figure; a structure.content top-level media node = standalone) — a different classification method than the raw census's ancestor-chain walk, so most of the cross-bucket shift versus the raw breakdown (e.g. para-inline 234 vs raw 214) is a labeling artifact, not a count error. Part of the para-inline excess is NOT an artifact, though: 5 of those para-inline segments are the genuine double-emission documented in otherResidualEffects below (a real fingerprint, not classification noise). The TOTAL (956) is exact and unambiguous either way.

structurallyUnreachableInCurrentCode.breakdownAttributionNote: Attributed by DIRECT parent, not 'any ancestor in chain' — corrected 2026-08-15 after review. An earlier pass of this artifact attributed by chain-membership (chain.includes('example') checked before chain.includes('note')) and reported 114/1; that mislabels 9 media whose direct, proximate parent is a <note> that happens to sit inside an <example> — the code path that actually fails to walk them is processNote (called explicitly by processExample for notes it contains), not processExample itself. The SUM is unchanged (105+10=115=114+1); only the two labels move.
structurallyUnreachableInCurrentCode.mechanism: Pre-existing gaps in tools/cnxml-extract.js, orthogonal to §C81 and predating this branch — the WHOLE <media> element (image + alt), not just the alt, has never been visible to the extracted structure at these four sites. processTable() calls extractInlineText(entry.content, mathMap, counters) with only 3 args, never threading inlineMediaMap, so the inline-media branch (gated `if (inlineMediaMap)`) never fires and a table-cell <media> is stripped as plain text with zero trace — this bucket is really 'in an <entry> and not in a <figure>': in chemistry all 29 <media alt> that sit in an <entry> have no nested <figure> (0 overlap, verified), so the bucket total (29) is the same either way — chemistry's 'entry' and 'entry-not-figure' counts happen to coincide. Organic is the one where the two labels diverge (see below). processExample() and processNote() only walk <para>/<list>/<equation>/(<note>) children — a bare <media> sibling (not wrapped in <figure> or <para>) is invisible to them, whichever of the two is its direct parent. emitExerciseSection()'s orderedExerciseBlocks() only returns <para> and sibling <list> blocks — a bare <media> sibling among <problem>/<solution> content is never collected. Verified empirically: none of these 197 elements' ids or alt text appear anywhere in extractSegments()'s output (structure JSON or segments array) for any of the 149 chemistry modules.

otherResidualEffects.arithmeticCheck: 1149 (raw) − 197 (structurally unreachable) + 4 (net residual) = 956 = measured emitted total. Fully reconciled, no unexplained residual.

duplicateAltSegmentIds.measuredBy: counting id-multiplicity directly on extractSegments().segments.filter(s=>s.type==='alt') for all 149 modules; cross-checked by an independent duplicate-TEXT scan on the same population, which agrees exactly (5 modules->2, 5 instances->5).
duplicateAltSegmentIds.significance: ⚠️ CORRECTS a recorded '0 of 491 real modules' (task-3-report.md Finding 2; task-4-report.md; progress.md line 112) — CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS 2026-08-15 after review. The prior '0' was NOT measuring too narrowly — Task 3 ran the SAME broad, corpus-wide duplicate-alt-text sweep (491 modules) this artifact uses, and it genuinely found 0 AT ITS OWN VINTAGE (commit 3ae61b7f). The real failure is a STALE RESTATEMENT across vintages: Task 4 (commit 326cb936) introduced the drain mechanism that immediately produces duplicate alt emissions (per review's vintage sweep: 20 at 326cb936, 21 by 4fe2b5f3, still 21 at dc11a5c8 — I independently corroborated only one endpoint, checking out pre-branch commit 40d0f0d4 and finding 0 duplicate ids of any type in both flagged modules, consistent with the 3ae61b7f→0 reading) — but Task 8's report (dc11a5c8) re-quotes Task 3's old '0 of 491' verbatim from a test's own docstring (`'pins a PRE-EXISTING double-extraction defect (see ledger; fires on 0 of 491 real modules)'`) instead of re-measuring at its own vintage, and that stale number then propagated into progress.md:112. The 5 chemistry duplicates ARE real and reachable, and post-date Task 3's correct '0'. Duplicate seg-ids are a tracked defect class in this repo (checkDuplicateSegIds, tools/lib/extraction-coverage.js) — parseSegmentsMap dedupes 'first', so the SECOND copy of each duplicate id is a silent inject drop, not a harmless repeat. §C80 re-extracts wholesale and freezes these ids, so this is worth carrying into the register as a named follow-up, not just prose here.

otherResidualEffects.walkIsLegacyButDuplicatesAreNew: ⚠️ IMPORTANT DISTINCTION, added after review: the WALK mechanism that causes double-extraction (extractInlineText re-matching media the caller has already handled a different way) is legacy — but its observable effect on ALT segments is NOT pre-existing; it is MATERIALISED by this branch. Verified directly against commit 40d0f0d4 (pre-branch, before any §C81 alt-segmentation existed): m68739 had ZERO duplicate segment ids of any type; m68764 had zero duplicate ALT ids but DID already have one pre-existing duplicate PARA id (m68764:para:fs-idm166392576, unrelated to alt). The redundant-walk pattern itself predates this branch (proven by that pre-existing para-id duplicate), but no duplicate ALT id existed before Task 4 added alt-segmentation to the positions that walk touches. Do not file this as purely legacy debt to deprioritize — it is new, branch-introduced behavior on a hot path §C80 is about to freeze.
doubleExtractionExamples: m68739.cnxml: a <list> nested inside a <para> that is a direct child of <example> is processed TWICE — once via the para's own flattened inline text (extractInlineText + drainInlineMediaAlts), and again via processExample's separate extractNestedElements(example.content,'list') + processList() walk over the same list. 4 media alts emitted twice each under the SAME segment id (net +4).

m68764.cnxml: a <figure> nested inside a <para> that is a direct child of <problem> is processed twice — once via global figure extraction (extractNestedElements(content,'figure') -> processFigure, which runs regardless of nesting), and again because the para's own inline-media regex matches the media even though it sits inside a nested <figure>. 1 media alt emitted twice under the SAME segment id (net +1).

Both sit in the SAME 'double-extraction' WALK-mechanism family task-3-report.md (Finding 2) first documented — but that report's own broad sweep, run at ITS vintage (commit 3ae61b7f, before Task 4 existed), correctly found 0 duplicate alt emissions in the whole corpus. These 5 chemistry duplicates were introduced when Task 4 (326cb936) added alt-segmentation to the code paths the legacy walk already touched — see walkIsLegacyButDuplicatesAreNew.
otherResidualEffects.regexTruncationExample: m68727.cnxml, figure id CNX_Chem_05_03_Systemqw / media id fs-idp1427264: the alt text contains a literal, unescaped '>' character mid-string ('...the terms "ΔU > 0", ...'). processFigure's mediaMatch regex `<media[^>]*>` stops at that literal character inside the attribute value, truncating the match before the tag's real closing '>'. The subsequent parseAttributes() call on the truncated fragment never finds a closing quote for alt="...", so mediaAttrs.alt parses as undefined, altText becomes '', and the segment is silently never emitted (no error) — confirmed against extractSegments()'s actual output (the segment id is absent). This is the SAME single instance the design spec already flagged (§4: 'entity-bearing alt is 1 of 1,149 in chemistry ... probably regex over-match'), now precisely diagnosed. ⚠️ RENDER-SIDE IMPACT NOW CONFIRMED, not just a risk: tools/lib/cnxml-parser.js's extractElements/extractNestedElements (consumed by cnxml-render.js's renderMedia path) share the identical `[^>]*`-stops-at-first-'>' shape. Directly verified: calling extractNestedElements on this figure's raw block returns attributes = {id: 'fs-idp1427264'} only — no 'alt' key at all, not even a truncated one. Today's published page (if this module is deployed) would render this figure with NO alt attribute — reader-visible, not merely untranslated. Pre-existing; out of scope to fix in Task 9, but should be logged as reader-facing, not just an extraction-side gap.

lifraen-efnafraedi_preview.scope: preview (17 of 342 source modules — the modules with extracted segments already present in 02-for-mt/, per this book's current onboarding state)

rawMediaAltCensus.note: Exact match to the design spec's organic-preview row (§1: 100/0/32, sum 132). All 32 non-figure media are id-less table-entry media (see below), consistent with the design's own 'id-less: 32' note.

emittedAltSegments.note: Same classification caveat as chemistry's block: byPosition here is attributed from structure.inlineMedia[]/figure/standalone content nodes, not the raw ancestor-chain walk. The design spec's own census says organic has ZERO para-inline media (rawMediaAltCensus.byPosition.para-inline = 0 above) — the 4 emitted 'para-inline' segments here are NOT a classification artifact, they ARE the double-extraction residual (see fullCorpusReconciliation and otherResidualEffects.duplicateAltTextInstances below): a <figure> nested in a <para> gets captured once correctly (counted under 'figure') and a second time via the para's own inline-media path (counted under 'para-inline'), so all 4 of this book's 'para-inline' entries are the extra, unwanted copies, not legitimate para-inline media.

structurallyUnreachableInCurrentCode.breakdownNote: All 32 of organic-preview's <entry>-nested alt media have no nested <figure> (0 overlap, verified) — the 'in an entry' and 'in an entry and not in a figure' counts coincide here. Organic's FULL 342-module corpus has exactly 1 counter-example (1 of 246 entry-nested media IS also in a figure and IS captured) — see fullCorpusReconciliation below; that one case falls outside the 17-module preview.
structurallyUnreachableInCurrentCode.mechanism: Same processTable()/extractInlineText 3-arg-call gap as chemistry's table-entry case. All 32 of organic's non-figure in-scope alts are id-less table-entry media (a functional-groups reference table in m00032), which is why the design's own census filed them as 'standalone, id-less' rather than distinguishing a table-entry bucket.
structurallyUnreachableInCurrentCode.severityNote: 31 of these 32 cells contain ONLY the <media> (no other text) — extractInlineText produces empty text, so the cell's segmentId is null and cnxml-inject.js's buildTable() falls through to its final branch, which preserves the entry verbatim from the original CNXML. The image still renders; only its alt stays English (same severity class as the rest of §C81's known gap). ONE cell (id-less, alt 'The general structure of halide...', alongside literal text '(X=F, Cl, Br, I)' in the same <entry>) is MIXED text+media — that cell DOES have a segmentId, so buildTable's earlier branch replaces the whole entry's content with just the translated text, which would silently drop the <media> (and its image) from the published table entirely. This is a materially more severe, single-instance defect, also pre-existing and out of scope here — flagged for the register.

otherResidualEffects.arithmeticCheck: 132 (raw) − 32 (structurally unreachable) + 4 (net residual) = 104 = measured emitted total. Fully reconciled, no unexplained residual.

duplicateAltSegmentIds.note: 0, NOT because the double-extraction defect is absent here — organic's media are id-less (altElementId falls back to positional `${kind}-${index}-alt` ids), so a double emission produces two DIFFERENT positional ids rather than a colliding duplicate id. The id-based check is structurally blind to this book's version of the defect; measured by duplicate-TEXT instead (below).

combined_491_modules.explanation: The 422-count gap is NOT a units mismatch, a missed module, an empty/whitespace alt, or a raw grep-vs-parse artifact (all of Task 9's candidate explanations were checked and ruled out except one). It IS exactly 'alt inside a structure whose extraction path still drops it': 442 alt-bearing <media> elements across the 491-module corpus sit in FOUR structural positions the current extractor cannot reach at all (table-entry-and-not-figure cells: 274 = 29 chem + 245 organic; bare media with <example> as direct parent: 105, chem only; bare media directly in <problem>/<solution>: 53, chem only; bare media with <note> as direct parent: 10, chem only — see each book's structurallyUnreachableInCurrentCode for the corrected, direct-parent attribution), partially offset by a MEASURED (not estimated) +21 double-extraction instances across the 491-module population (5 in chemistry's 149 modules + 16 in organic's full 342 modules — organic-preview's +4 is a SUBSET of that 16, not additive on top of it — all confirmed by exact duplicate-id or duplicate-text counts on real extractSegments() output) and one regex-truncation drop in the opposite direction (−1, chem, m68727). Arithmetic: 442 − 21 + 1 = 422 — EXACT match to the measured gap, no unexplained residual. CORRECTED 2026-08-15 after review: mechanism 1 (structurally unreachable) is genuinely pre-existing and orthogonal to §C81. Mechanism 2 is NOT — only the underlying redundant-WALK is legacy; the duplicate ALT ids/text it produces are NEW, introduced when Task 4 (this branch) added alt-segmentation to the code paths that walk already touched (verified against pre-branch commit 40d0f0d4: zero duplicate alt ids existed anywhere in either flagged module before Task 4 landed). §C81 adds alt-segmentation only to positions the extractor was already structurally reaching (figure / para-inline / top-level standalone) — that part is correct — but doing so also newly exposed a pre-existing walk defect as visible, reader-facing duplicate segments, which is a §C81-introduced regression in observable effect even though the walk mechanism itself predates the branch.

schemaNote: Field/key shapes deliberately diverge from the brief's illustrative Step-1 script (which used a flat `altSegments` count and the bare book slug as key): `emittedAltSegments.total` vs `rawMediaAltCensus.total` are kept as separate, clearly-named siblings because the two counting units must never be read as interchangeable (see countingUnits above) — a flat `altSegments` field would silently pick one and hide the other. `lifraen-efnafraedi_preview` (vs bare `lifraen-efnafraedi`) is used as the book key specifically so it sits alongside `lifraen-efnafraedi_FULL_342_modules_NOT_in_scope` under fullCorpusReconciliation without a naming collision. Nothing currently reads this file programmatically; §C82 (named as its eventual consumer in the plan) should either adopt this shape or this file should be adapted to whatever shape §C82 needs — the rename here was a deliberate clarity choice for THIS artifact, not a contract yet negotiated with a consumer.
notes: In-scope numbers do NOT match the brief's ~1,149/~132 expectation when measured as EMITTED SEGMENTS (956/104) — but DO match exactly when measured as the RAW <media>-with-alt CENSUS (1,149/132), which is what the design spec's own number actually is. Both numbers are correct for what they measure; they are not interchangeable, and the brief's own Step 1 script computes the emitted-segment number while quoting the raw-census expectation. The 193/28-count shortfall within the IN-SCOPE population (not just the out-of-scope full-491 population) is real, reproducible, and traced to specific named code paths in tools/cnxml-extract.js (table-entry-not-figure cells; bare media in <example>/<problem>/<solution>/<note>, attributed by DIRECT parent — see each book's structurallyUnreachableInCurrentCode) that predate §C81 and are out of its stated scope — §C81 adds alt-segmentation only to the three positions (figure/para-inline/top-level-standalone) the extractor was already structurally visiting; it does not expand extraction coverage itself. This mechanism is a pre-existing gap, not a §C81 regression. A SECOND finding surfaced during reconciliation and corrects a previously recorded '0 of 491' for the 'double-extraction' defect class — CORRECTED 2026-08-15 after review: the prior '0' (task-3-report.md) was measured correctly at ITS OWN vintage (commit 3ae61b7f, before Task 4 existed); the failure was a STALE RESTATEMENT of that number in later reports (task-4-report.md; progress.md:112; task-8-report.md, dc11a5c8) made without re-measuring after Task 4 changed the code. The defect actually fires on 14 real modules (5 duplicate alt-segment emissions in 2 chemistry modules with colliding ids — a tracked defect class, checkDuplicateSegIds — plus 16 duplicate-text emissions in 12 organic modules, out of organic's full 342-module corpus, where id-less media hide the collision from an id-based check; 4 of those 16 fall within the 17-module in-scope preview), and — unlike the first finding — this one is NOT purely pre-existing: the underlying redundant walk is legacy, but the duplicate ALT ids/text are newly materialized by this branch (verified 0 existed at pre-branch commit 40d0f0d4). A THIRD, smaller finding was upgraded from risk to confirmed: m68727's regex-truncated alt is dropped not only from extraction but also from cnxml-render.js's rendering path (directly verified — parses with no 'alt' key at all), so today's published page (if deployed) shows this figure with no alt attribute, reader-visible. All three findings should be logged in the active register as follow-up scope before §C80's wholesale re-extraction freezes these ids; none was fixed here (measurement-only task, no production code changed).
